L2925@P69: COMBINING ACTIVE AND METRIC LEARNING FOR HYPERSPECTRAL IMAGE CLASSIFICATION
L2926@P69: Edoardo Pasolli, Hsiuhan Lexie Yang and Melba M. Crawford,
L2927@P69: School of Civil Engineering, Purdue University, USA
L2928@P69: Abstract : Classification of hyperspectral remote sensing images is affected by two main problems: high dimensionality
L2929@P69: of the acquired signatures and scarce availability of labeled samples. Learning a low dimensional manifold and active learning
L2930@P69: represent two approaches that have been investigated in the literature to mitigate these effects. However they are usually applied
L2931@P69: independently from each other. In this paper we propose a method in which feature extraction and active learning are combined.
L2932@P69: In particular, a new reduced feature space is learned by large margin nearest neighbor (LMNN), a metric learning strategy that
L2933@P69: takes advantage of labeled information. The method is applied in conjunction with k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) classification, for
L2934@P69: which a new sample selection strategy is proposed. Experiments on a real hyperspectral dataset confirm the effectiveness of the
L2935@P69: proposed method.
L2936@P69: HYPERSPECTRAL CLASSIFICATION USING STACKED AUTOENCODERS WITH DEEP LEARNING
L2937@P69: A. Okan Bilge Özdemir, B. Ekin Gedik and C. Yasemin Yardımcı Çetin,
L2938@P69: Middle East Technical University Informatics Institute Ankara, Turkey
L2939@P69: Abstract : In this study, stacked autoencoders which are widely utilized in deep learning research are applied to remote
L2940@P69: sensing domain for hyperspectral classification. High dimensional hyperspectral data is an excellent candidate for deep learning methods. However, there are no works in literature that focuses on such deep learning approaches for hyperspectral imagery.
L2941@P69: This study aims to fill this gap by utilizing stacked autoencoders. Experiments are conducted on the Pavia University scene. Using
L2942@P69: stacked autoencoders, intrinsic representations of the data are learned in an unsupervised way. Using labeled data, these representations are fine tuned. Then, using a soft-max activation function, hyperspectral classification is done. Parameter optimization of
L2943@P69: Stacked Autoencoders (SAE) is done with extensive experiments. Results are competitive with the state-of-the-art techniques.
